```{r Step 0: Data Ingestion, include=TRUE}
gss_analysis <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "GSS_Data_Cleaned", "gss_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"))
composite_measure_base <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"))
```


```{r Step 1: Diagnosing Coverage of Measures, include=TRUE}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.1 Define the common industry universe
# ------------------------------------------------------------

common_industries <- c(
  "Construction",
  "Manufacturing",
  "Wholesale trade",
  "Retail trade",
  "Transportation and warehousing",
  "Information",
  "Finance and insurance",
  "Real estate and rental and leasing",
  "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
  "Administrative and support and waste management",
  "Educational services",
  "Health care and social assistance",
  "Leisure and hospitality",
  "Other services"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.2 Define the measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_measures <- c(
  "wage_premium",
  "wage_cost_per_hour",
  "benefits_nonrequired",
  "layoffs_discharge_rate",
  "earnings_volatility"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.3 Basic structure of the industry-year panel
# ------------------------------------------------------------

composite_measure_base %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# Confirm that the panel contains exactly the intended
# common-industry universe

composite_measure_base %>%
  distinct(industry_common) %>%
  anti_join(
    tibble(industry_common = common_industries),
    by = "industry_common"
  )


# Confirm that each industry-year is unique

composite_measure_base %>%
  count(year, industry_common) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.4 SOURCE-LEVEL TEMPORAL COVERAGE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

source_coverage <- composite_measure_base %>%
  summarise(
    wage_premium_first_year =
      min(year[!is.na(wage_premium)], na.rm = TRUE),

    wage_premium_last_year =
      max(year[!is.na(wage_premium)], na.rm = TRUE),

    wage_cost_first_year =
      min(year[!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)], na.rm = TRUE),

    wage_cost_last_year =
      max(year[!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)], na.rm = TRUE),

    benefits_first_year =
      min(year[!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)], na.rm = TRUE),

    benefits_last_year =
      max(year[!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)], na.rm = TRUE),

    stability_first_year =
      min(year[!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)], na.rm = TRUE),

    stability_last_year =
      max(year[!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)], na.rm = TRUE),

    volatility_first_year =
      min(year[!is.na(earnings_volatility)], na.rm = TRUE),

    volatility_last_year =
      max(year[!is.na(earnings_volatility)], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

source_coverage


# A more useful long-format version

source_temporal_coverage <- composite_measure_base %>%
  summarise(
    wage_premium = list(year[!is.na(wage_premium)]),
    wage_cost_per_hour = list(year[!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)]),
    benefits_nonrequired = list(year[!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)]),
    layoffs_discharge_rate = list(year[!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)]),
    earnings_volatility = list(year[!is.na(earnings_volatility)])
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "years"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    first_year = map_int(years, min),
    last_year = map_int(years, max),
    n_years = map_int(years, ~ n_distinct(.x))
  ) %>%
  select(
    measure,
    first_year,
    last_year,
    n_years
  )

source_temporal_coverage


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.5 SOURCE-LEVEL COVERAGE BY INDUSTRY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_source_coverage <- composite_measure_base %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n(),

    wage_premium_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_premium)),

    wage_cost_per_hour_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    benefits_nonrequired_n =
      sum(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)),

    layoffs_discharge_rate_n =
      sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    earnings_volatility_n =
      sum(!is.na(earnings_volatility)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_common)

industry_source_coverage


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.6 CREATE A BINARY INDUSTRY × MEASURE COVERAGE MATRIX
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_coverage_matrix <- composite_measure_base %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    wage_premium =
      any(!is.na(wage_premium)),

    wage_cost_per_hour =
      any(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    benefits_nonrequired =
      any(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)),

    layoffs_discharge_rate =
      any(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    earnings_volatility =
      any(!is.na(earnings_volatility)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_common)

industry_coverage_matrix


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.7 RESPONDENT-LEVEL COVERAGE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_coverage <- gss_analysis %>%
  summarise(
    n_gss = n(),

    industry_missing =
      sum(is.na(industry_common)),

    industry_missing_pct =
      mean(is.na(industry_common)) * 100,

    wage_premium_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_premium)),

    wage_premium_pct =
      mean(!is.na(wage_premium)) * 100,

    wage_cost_per_hour_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    wage_cost_per_hour_pct =
      mean(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)) * 100,

    benefits_nonrequired_n =
      sum(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)),

    benefits_nonrequired_pct =
      mean(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)) * 100,

    layoffs_discharge_rate_n =
      sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    layoffs_discharge_rate_pct =
      mean(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)) * 100,

    earnings_volatility_n =
      sum(!is.na(earnings_volatility)),

    earnings_volatility_pct =
      mean(!is.na(earnings_volatility)) * 100
  )

gss_coverage

# 1.8 RESPONDENT COVERAGE BY INDUSTRY

gss_industry_coverage <- gss_analysis %>%

gss_year_coverage


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.10 COVERAGE OF THE COMPLETE FOUR-DIMENSION MEASURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Here we distinguish the four conceptual dimensions:
#
# Compensation = wage premium + ECEC wage
# Benefits = ECEC benefits
# Stability = JOLTS layoffs/discharges
# Earnings stability = QWI earnings volatility
#
# For now, require the components within each dimension
# to be available.

gss_analysis <- gss_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    has_compensation =
      !is.na(wage_premium) &
      !is.na(wage_cost_per_hour),

    has_benefits =
      !is.na(benefits_nonrequired),

    has_stability =
      !is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate),

    has_earnings_stability =
      !is.na(earnings_volatility),

    has_all_four_dimensions =
      has_compensation &
      has_benefits &
      has_stability &
      has_earnings_stability
  )


# Overall coverage

gss_analysis %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    compensation_n =
      sum(has_compensation),

    compensation_pct =
      mean(has_compensation) * 100,

    benefits_n =
      sum(has_benefits),

    benefits_pct =
      mean(has_benefits) * 100,

    stability_n =
      sum(has_stability),

    stability_pct =
      mean(has_stability) * 100,

    earnings_stability_n =
      sum(has_earnings_stability),

    earnings_stability_pct =
      mean(has_earnings_stability) * 100,

    all_four_dimensions_n =
      sum(has_all_four_dimensions),

    all_four_dimensions_pct =
      mean(has_all_four_dimensions) * 100
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.11 COVERAGE OF THE COMPLETE MEASURE BY INDUSTRY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_analysis %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

  ) %>%

#The objective job-quality measures can be assigned to approximately 86% of GSS respondents with an identifiable industry. Compensation and benefits measures are available for approximately 73% of respondents because the ECEC series begins in 2004. The complete four-dimension measure is available for approximately 52% of respondents overall and, among survey years from 2004 onward, for approximately 59–64% of respondents. The primary constraint on complete coverage is the availability of detailed JOLTS layoffs/discharges data for only a subset of the common industry classifications.
```

```{r Step 2, Summary Distributions for Components of Composite Measure, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# STEP 3: DISTRIBUTIONS AND SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================

# Measures to inspect
job_quality_measures <- c(
  "wage_premium",
  "wage_cost_per_hour",
  "benefits_nonrequired",
  "layoffs_discharge_rate",
  "earnings_volatility"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3A. OVERALL SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_summary <- composite_measure_base %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(job_quality_measures),
      list(
        n = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
        mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        p01 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
        p05 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
        p25 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        p75 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
        p95 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
        p99 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),

# ============================================================
# Correlation Analysis of Job Quality Measures
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the five indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_measures <- c(
  "wage_premium",
  "wage_cost_per_hour",
  "benefits_nonrequired",
  "layoffs_discharge_rate",
  "earnings_volatility"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Matrix 1: Raw five indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the original measures exactly as they appear in the
# industry-year dataset.

cor_raw <- composite_measure_base %>%
  select(all_of(job_quality_measures)) %>%
  cor(
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
    method = "pearson"
  )

cor_raw


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Matrix 2: Directionally aligned indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Reverse the two measures where higher values indicate
# worse job quality:
#
#   layoffs/discharges -> lower is better
#   earnings volatility -> lower is better
#
# After this transformation, higher values consistently
# indicate better job quality.

cor_aligned_data <- composite_measure_base %>%
  transmute(
    wage_premium = wage_premium,
    wage_cost_per_hour = wage_cost_per_hour,
    benefits_nonrequired = benefits_nonrequired,
    stability = -layoffs_discharge_rate,
    earnings_stability = -earnings_volatility
  )

cor_aligned <- cor(
  cor_aligned_data,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_aligned


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Matrix 3: Standardized, directionally aligned indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Standardize each indicator to mean = 0 and SD = 1.
#
# Because correlation is invariant to linear rescaling,
# these correlations will numerically be the same as Matrix 2.
# The purpose of this matrix is primarily to establish the
# standardized variables that will later be used to construct
# the composite JQI.

cor_standardized_data <- cor_aligned_data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))
    )
  )

cor_standardized <- cor(
  cor_standardized_data,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

cor_standardized


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Make the matrices easier to read
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cor_raw_named <- cor_raw

cor_aligned_named <- cor_aligned
colnames(cor_aligned_named) <- c(
  "Wage premium",
  "ECEC wage",
  "Benefits",
  "Stability",
  "Earnings stability"
)
rownames(cor_aligned_named) <- colnames(cor_aligned_named)

cor_standardized_named <- cor_standardized
colnames(cor_standardized_named) <- c(
  "Wage premium",
  "ECEC wage",
  "Benefits",
  "Stability",
  "Earnings stability"
)
rownames(cor_standardized_named) <- colnames(cor_standardized_named)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Print all three matrices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("MATRIX 1: RAW INDICATORS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
print(round(cor_raw, 3))


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("MATRIX 2: DIRECTIONALLY ALIGNED INDICATORS\n")
cat("Higher values = better job quality\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
print(round(cor_aligned_named, 3))


cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("MATRIX 3: STANDARDIZED + DIRECTIONALLY ALIGNED INDICATORS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
print(round(cor_standardized_named, 3))



```

```{r Step 4, Work on Constructing the Composite Measure, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# Construction of Four-Dimension Job Quality Index
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create standardized, directionally aligned indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions <- composite_measure_base %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Compensation indicators
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),
    z_ecec_wage = as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),
    
    # Benefits
    z_benefits = as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),
    
    # Employment stability:
    # reverse layoffs/discharges so higher = better
    z_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-layoffs_discharge_rate)
    ),
    
    # Earnings stability:
    # reverse earnings volatility so higher = better
    z_earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Construct the four substantive dimensions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Dimension 1: Compensation
    # Equal weight to wage premium and ECEC wage
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_ecec_wage
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Dimension 2: Benefits
    benefits = z_benefits,
    
    # Dimension 3: Employment stability
    stability = z_stability,
    
    # Dimension 4: Earnings stability
    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct the overall Job Quality Index
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Equal weight to the four substantive dimensions.
#
# The JQI is defined only when all four dimensions are
# available for a given industry-year.

job_quality_dimensions <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  mutate(
    
    jqi = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        stability,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Standardize the final JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# jqi = substantively constructed index
#
# jqi_z = standardized version of the final index.
# A one-unit increase in jqi_z represents a one-standard-
# deviation increase in objective job quality.

job_quality_dimensions <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_z = as.numeric(scale(jqi))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Summarize the four dimensions and JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimension_summary <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    
    compensation_n = sum(!is.na(compensation)),
    compensation_mean = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation_sd = sd(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    benefits_n = sum(!is.na(benefits)),
    benefits_mean = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits_sd = sd(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    stability_n = sum(!is.na(stability)),
    stability_mean = mean(stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    stability_sd = sd(stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    earnings_stability_n = sum(!is.na(earnings_stability)),
    earnings_stability_mean = mean(
      earnings_stability,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    earnings_stability_sd = sd(
      earnings_stability,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    jqi_mean = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_sd = sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_z_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_z)),
    jqi_z_mean = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_z_sd = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

job_quality_dimension_summary


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Correlation matrix of the four dimensions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dimension_data <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  select(
    compensation,
    benefits,
    stability,
    earnings_stability
  )

dimension_correlations <- cor(
  dimension_data,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

dimension_correlations_named <- dimension_correlations

colnames(dimension_correlations_named) <- c(
  "Compensation",
  "Benefits",
  "Employment stability",
  "Earnings stability"
)

  dimension_correlations_named
)

    p05 = quantile(jqi, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    p25 = quantile(jqi, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),

    p95 = quantile(jqi, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99 = quantile(jqi, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),

jqi_summary
```

```{r Step 5: Diagnostic Work on the Composite Measure, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# STAGE 1: MECHANICAL VALIDATION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Basic JQI coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_coverage <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    total_industry_years = n(),
    
    compensation_n = sum(!is.na(compensation)),

    stability_n = sum(!is.na(stability)),
    earnings_stability_n = sum(!is.na(earnings_stability)),
    
    jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    jqi_z_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_z)),
    
    jqi_missing = sum(is.na(jqi)),
    jqi_z_missing = sum(is.na(jqi_z))
  )

print(jqi_coverage)

jqi_standardization_check <- job_quality_dimensions %>%

    jqi_mean = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),

print(jqi_standardization_check)

dimension_summary <- job_quality_dimensions %>%

    ),

      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

print(dimension_summary)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Correlations between dimensions and JQI

dimension_jqi_correlations <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  select(

  ) %>%

# ============================================================
# STAGE 2: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Construct leave-one-dimension-out indices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_sensitivity <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Remove compensation
    jqi_no_compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        benefits,
        stability,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Remove benefits
    jqi_no_benefits = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        stability,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Remove employment stability
    jqi_no_stability = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Remove earnings stability
    jqi_no_earnings_stability = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Correlation of alternative indices with main JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_sensitivity_correlations <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  select(
    jqi,
    jqi_no_compensation,
    jqi_no_benefits,
    jqi_no_stability,
    jqi_no_earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  cor(
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
  )

print(round(jqi_sensitivity_correlations, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Standardized alternative indices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_sensitivity <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_no_compensation_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_no_compensation)),
    
    jqi_no_benefits_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_no_benefits)),
    
    jqi_no_stability_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_no_stability)),
    
    jqi_no_earnings_stability_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_no_earnings_stability))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Rank correlations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_rank_correlations <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  select(
    jqi,
    jqi_no_compensation,
    jqi_no_benefits,
    jqi_no_stability,
    jqi_no_earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  cor(
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
    method = "spearman"
  )

print(round(jqi_rank_correlations, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Compare industry rankings across specifications
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_industry_sensitivity <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    
    jqi = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_no_compensation =
      mean(jqi_no_compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_no_benefits =
      mean(jqi_no_benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_no_stability =
      mean(jqi_no_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    jqi_no_earnings_stability =
      mean(jqi_no_earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    
    rank_jqi = rank(
      -jqi,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_no_compensation = rank(
      -jqi_no_compensation,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_no_benefits = rank(
      -jqi_no_benefits,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_no_stability = rank(
      -jqi_no_stability,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_no_earnings_stability = rank(
      -jqi_no_earnings_stability,
      ties.method = "average"
    )
  )

print(jqi_industry_sensitivity)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Rank changes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_industry_rank_changes <- jqi_industry_sensitivity %>%
  transmute(
    industry_common,
    rank_jqi,
    rank_no_compensation,
    rank_no_benefits,
    rank_no_stability,
    rank_no_earnings_stability,
    
    change_no_compensation =
      rank_no_compensation - rank_jqi,
    
    change_no_benefits =
      rank_no_benefits - rank_jqi,
    
    change_no_stability =
      rank_no_stability - rank_jqi,
    
    change_no_earnings_stability =
      rank_no_earnings_stability - rank_jqi
  )

print(jqi_industry_rank_changes)


# ============================================================
# ALTERNATIVE JQI: EQUAL WEIGHT TO FIVE UNDERLYING INDICATORS
# ============================================================

# Main JQI:
#   25% Compensation
#   25% Benefits
#   25% Employment stability
#   25% Earnings stability
#
# Alternative JQI:
#   20% Wage premium
#   20% ECEC wage
#   20% Benefits
#   20% Employment stability
#   20% Earnings stability
#
# All five indicators are already standardized and directionally
# aligned in job_quality_dimensions.


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Construct alternative five-indicator JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_sensitivity <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    
    jqi_equal_indicators = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_ecec_wage,
        z_benefits,
        z_stability,
        z_earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Standardize alternative JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_sensitivity <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_equal_indicators_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_equal_indicators))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Basic comparison with main JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_comparison <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  summarise(
    
    main_jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    alternative_jqi_n =
      sum(!is.na(jqi_equal_indicators)),
    
    main_jqi_mean =
      mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    main_jqi_sd =
      sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    alternative_jqi_mean =
      mean(jqi_equal_indicators, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    alternative_jqi_sd =
      sd(jqi_equal_indicators, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    alternative_jqi_z_mean =
      mean(jqi_equal_indicators_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    alternative_jqi_z_sd =
      sd(jqi_equal_indicators_z, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

jqi_weighting_comparison


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Pearson correlation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_pearson <- cor(
  job_quality_sensitivity %>%
    select(
      jqi,
      jqi_equal_indicators
    ),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(round(jqi_weighting_pearson, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Spearman rank correlation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_spearman <- cor(
  job_quality_sensitivity %>%
    select(
      jqi,
      jqi_equal_indicators
    ),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "spearman"
)

print(round(jqi_weighting_spearman, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Compare industry-level rankings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_industry <- job_quality_sensitivity %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    
    n_main = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    n_alternative =
      sum(!is.na(jqi_equal_indicators)),
    
    mean_jqi =
      mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_jqi_equal_indicators =
      mean(
        jqi_equal_indicators,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    
    rank_main = rank(
      -mean_jqi,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_equal_indicators = rank(
      -mean_jqi_equal_indicators,
      ties.method = "average"
    ),
    
    rank_change =
      rank_equal_indicators - rank_main
  )

jqi_weighting_industry


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Industry-level rank correlation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_industry_cor <- cor(
  jqi_weighting_industry %>%
    select(
      mean_jqi,
      mean_jqi_equal_indicators
    ),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "spearman"
)

jqi_weighting_industry_cor


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Identify largest changes in industry ranking
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_industry %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(rank_change)))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Compare standardized versions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_weighting_z_cor <- cor(
  job_quality_sensitivity %>%
    select(
      jqi_z,
      jqi_equal_indicators_z
    ),
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(round(jqi_weighting_z_cor, 3))





# ============================================================
# STAGE 3: STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Industry-level JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_industry <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_jqi_z = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_jqi))

jqi_industry


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Year-level JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_year <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_jqi_z = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year)

jqi_year


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Overall correlation between JQI and year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_year_correlation <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    correlation = cor(
      jqi,
      year,
      use = "complete.obs"
    )
  )

jqi_year_correlation


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Within-industry trajectories
# ------------------------------------------------------------


jqi_industry_trajectories <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi)) %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    first_jqi = jqi[year == min(year)][1],
    last_jqi = jqi[year == max(year)][1],
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi),
    change_first_to_last = last_jqi - first_jqi,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_jqi))


jqi_industry_trajectories


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Between-industry versus within-industry variation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Industry mean
jqi_variance_data <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  mutate(
    industry_mean_jqi = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    between_component =
      industry_mean_jqi,
    
    within_component =
      jqi - industry_mean_jqi
  )


# Between-industry variance
between_industry_variance <- jqi_variance_data %>%
  summarise(
    variance_between =
      var(
        industry_mean_jqi,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  )


# Within-industry variance
within_industry_variance <- jqi_variance_data %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    within_variance =
      var(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    variance_within =
      mean(
        within_variance,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  )


between_industry_variance
within_industry_variance


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Intraclass correlation coefficient
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ICC = between-industry variance /
#       (between-industry variance + within-industry variance)

icc_jqi <- between_industry_variance$variance_between /
  (
    between_industry_variance$variance_between +
      within_industry_variance$variance_within
  )

icc_jqi


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. More direct variance decomposition
# ------------------------------------------------------------

overall_variance <- var(
  jqi_variance_data$jqi,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

between_variance <- between_industry_variance$variance_between

within_variance <- within_industry_variance$variance_within

variance_decomposition <- tibble(
  component = c(
    "Between industry",
    "Within industry",
    "Total"
  ),
  
  variance = c(
    between_variance,
    within_variance,
    overall_variance
  ),
  
  percent_total = c(
    100 * between_variance / overall_variance,
    100 * within_variance / overall_variance,
    100
  )
)

variance_decomposition

#The JQI exhibits substantial and persistent differences across industries while also capturing meaningful changes in job quality within industries over time. Approximately 73% of observed JQI variation is between industries and 28% is within industries, with an ICC of 0.73. The measure therefore reflects both structural differences in the quality of employment opportunities across industries and historically varying labor-market conditions within industries.


# ============================================================
# STAGE 4: EXTERNAL AND CRITERION VALIDITY
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4A: JQI and its underlying dimensions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Start from the saved GSS job-quality dataset
gss_analysis <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

# Check that the merge keys exist
stopifnot(
  "year" %in% names(gss_analysis),
  "industry_common" %in% names(gss_analysis)
)

# Add the four JQI dimensions and composite measure
gss_analysis <- gss_analysis %>%
  left_join(
    job_quality_dimensions %>%
      select(
        year,
        industry_common,
        compensation,
        benefits,
        stability,
        earnings_stability,
        jqi,
        jqi_z
      ),
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  )

# Confirm that the JQI was actually added
print(
  gss_analysis %>%
    summarise(
      n_total = n(),
      n_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
      pct_jqi = 100 * mean(!is.na(jqi)),
      n_missing_jqi = sum(is.na(jqi)),
      pct_missing_jqi = 100 * mean(is.na(jqi))
    )
)



# Correlations between the JQI and its four substantive dimensions

jqi_dimension_validity <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  select(
    jqi,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    stability,
    earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  cor(
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
    method = "pearson"
  )

print(round(jqi_dimension_validity, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4B: Compare JQI against the individual indicators
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_indicator_validity <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  select(
    jqi,
    wage_premium,
    wage_cost_per_hour,
    benefits_nonrequired,
    layoffs_discharge_rate,
    earnings_volatility
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    layoffs_discharge_rate = -layoffs_discharge_rate,
    earnings_volatility = -earnings_volatility
  ) %>%
  cor(
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
    method = "pearson"
  )

print(round(jqi_indicator_validity, 3))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4C: Industry-level face/construct validity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Average JQI and its dimensions by industry.
# This allows us to see whether industries with higher overall
# JQI also exhibit the expected underlying characteristics.

jqi_industry_validity <- job_quality_dimensions %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi)) %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    jqi = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    stability = mean(stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    earnings_stability = mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(jqi))

print(jqi_industry_validity, n = 14)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4D: Rank-order validity across industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare the industry ranking implied by the JQI with each
# underlying dimension.

jqi_industry_rank_validity <- jqi_industry_validity %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_rank = rank(-jqi),
    compensation_rank = rank(-compensation),
    benefits_rank = rank(-benefits),
    stability_rank = rank(-stability),
    earnings_stability_rank = rank(-earnings_stability)
  )

print(jqi_industry_rank_validity, n = 14)


# Spearman correlations between the industry-level JQI ranking
# and each dimension's ranking.

industry_rank_correlations <- tibble(
  comparison = c(
    "Compensation",
    "Benefits",
    "Employment stability",
    "Earnings stability"
  ),
  spearman_rho = c(
    cor(
      jqi_industry_validity$jqi,
      jqi_industry_validity$compensation,
      method = "spearman"
    ),
    cor(
      jqi_industry_validity$jqi,
      jqi_industry_validity$benefits,
      method = "spearman"
    ),
    cor(
      jqi_industry_validity$jqi,
      jqi_industry_validity$stability,
      method = "spearman"
    ),
    cor(
      jqi_industry_validity$jqi,
      jqi_industry_validity$earnings_stability,
      method = "spearman"
    )
  )
)

print(industry_rank_correlations)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4E: Test whether the JQI is associated with subjective
# job-related outcomes in the GSS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# First, inspect the variables currently available in the GSS.
# This is intentionally diagnostic rather than assuming that
# particular variable names exist.

gss_job_quality_vars <- names(gss_analysis)

# Search for potentially relevant job satisfaction/security/
# employment-attitude variables.

gss_job_quality_candidates <- gss_job_quality_vars[
  str_detect(
    tolower(gss_job_quality_vars),
    "satis|secure|security|job|work|employ|income|financ"
  )
]

print(gss_job_quality_candidates)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4F: Coverage of the JQI in the GSS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Examine how many GSS respondents have a complete JQI.

gss_jqi_coverage <- gss_analysis %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    pct_jqi = 100 * mean(!is.na(jqi)),
    n_missing_jqi = sum(is.na(jqi)),
    pct_missing_jqi = 100 * mean(is.na(jqi))
  )

print(gss_jqi_coverage)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4G: Compare respondents with and without JQI coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# This is important because JOLTS coverage restricts the JQI
# to eight industries. We want to determine whether respondents
# with and without a JQI are systematically different.

gss_jqi_coverage_by_industry <- gss_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_available = !is.na(jqi)
  ) %>%
  count(industry_common, jqi_available) %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_within_industry = 100 * n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(gss_jqi_coverage_by_industry, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4H: Year-specific JQI coverage in the GSS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_year_coverage <- gss_analysis %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    pct_jqi = 100 * mean(!is.na(jqi)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(gss_jqi_year_coverage, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Stage 4I: Create analysis dataset for criterion-validity tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# This creates a clean dataset containing respondents with a
# complete JQI and the basic respondent characteristics needed
# for later criterion-validity models.

gss_jqi_analysis <- gss_analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi))
  

# Basic structure
glimpse(gss_jqi_analysis)

# Number of observations by year
gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  count(year) %>%
  print(n = 30)
```
